title: High-frequency payment records are Active Data edited directly by a named party, outside the Root Edit process
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.5.1.2.1.3.4 and A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.3.4 mark the payment lists for Spark's Distribution Reward and Integration Boost Instances as **Active Data**, with an identical control block: "The Responsible Party is Operational GovOps. The Update Process must follow the protocol for 'Direct Edit'."

This is a second write path into the Artifact. Everything discussed under the Root Edit Primitive — 1% proposal threshold, risk council review, facilitator alignment review, weekly poll — governs the *rules*. Active Data is the ledger those rules produce, and it is updated by a named operational role without any of that machinery.

The separation is necessary rather than a shortcut. Integration Boost payments run weekly (A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.1.4); routing each week's figures through a governance vote would be absurd, and treating them as ungoverned off-document data would break the Artifact's claim to be the complete specification.

The design cost is a class of Artifact content that a single accountable party can change unilaterally. The safeguards are structural rather than procedural: the Responsible Party is named in advance, the update protocol is fixed, and the data is the output of formulas defined in the governed sections — so a Direct Edit that does not follow from those formulas is checkable against them.

For readers of any Atlas document, the practical lesson is that document sections are typed. `[Core]` text and `[Active Data]` content are amendable by entirely different processes, and the tag is the only signal of which applies.
description: Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payment lists carry an Active Data Controller naming Operational GovOps as Responsible Party under a 'Direct Edit' protocol — no proposal or vote.
